assertion: The EIA forecasts U.S. crude oil production will average 13.8 million barrels per day (b/d) in 2026, surpassing the previous record of 13.7 million b/d set in 2025.
warehouse_value: 2025 actual avg 13,660 MBBL/D (13.66 mb/d); 2026 H1 actual avg 13,712 MBBL/D (13.71 mb/d)
sql: SELECT production_year, AVG(production_volume) FROM energy.eia_crude_oil_production WHERE eia_area_code='NUS' AND fuel_type='Crude Oil' AND production_unit='MBBL/D' GROUP BY production_year
reason: Directly matches the September 2026 STEO, the report the article names as its source, to the rounded decimal.

assertion: Marketed natural gas production will average 122.5 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d) in 2026, surpassing the previous record of 118.5 Bcf/d set in 2025.
warehouse_value: 2025 actual avg ~118.3 Bcf/d; 2026 H1 actual avg ~121.6 Bcf/d
sql: SELECT production_year, SUM(production_volume)/1000.0 AS total_bcf FROM energy.eia_natural_gas_production WHERE eia_area_code='NUS' AND process_code='VGM' GROUP BY production_year
independent_value: September 2026 STEO Table 5a: 2025 = 118.4 Bcf/d, 2026 forecast = 123.0 Bcf/d (not 118.5 / 122.5, which are the August 2026 STEO's figures)

sources.title: EIA Today in Energy, August 12, 2026 (source of the 122.5/118.5 figures, attributed to the August STEO)

reason: The 122.5/118.5 figures are real EIA STEO numbers but come from the August 2026 STEO, one release cycle before the September 2026 STEO the article cites; the September STEO revised these to 123.0/118.4.
